copy.title: CrimeMaps Germany
copy.caption: German police report maps · 14 cities
copy.note: Selected police announcements. They do not represent all crime.
copy.details: This is an early open-source version. Coverage, locations and translations may have gaps or errors. Please read the linked police announcements for context. Contributions are welcome.
copy.images: The city images were generated with AI using local landmarks. They introduce the cities and do not depict specific incidents.
copy.sourcesNote: POLIZEIKARTE is an independent project. The police links lead to the authorities responsible for each city.
copy.externalPoliceLabel: Open the police website for {city} (new window)
copy.githubPrivacy: To leave a message, sign in to GitHub. Your account and message are public. Do not include personal or sensitive information.
copy.analyticsCollection: GoatCounter counts page loads and reloads, excluding language changes and map operations. These are not unique visitors.
copy.analyticsOff: Visit collection is not enabled on this page.
copy.analyticsPrivacy: Country totals only. The connection IP is processed to estimate the country; individual pageviews, referrers and sessions are disabled.
copy.noticeProgress: The site is being improved. Announcement content is updated weekly; maps and nearby facilities (POIs) are updated monthly.
copy.noticeTranslation: GPT and Doubao Lite assist with translation. Chinese is the priority review version. English about 90% and German about 85% are project estimates, not results of a full accuracy assessment. Some details may still show the original text; check the source.
copy.noticeData: Selected police announcements and POLIZEIKARTE records retain source links. They are not a complete crime inventory; announcement totals are not counts of distinct offences.
copy.noticeMap: Hexagons summarize eligible announcements for the selected year; the month filters report lists and details. POI type colours and outlines provide geographic context. Small black Roman numerals I–XV below the centres convert the previous shading strength into 15 display bands; they are not announcement counts, offence counts or risk levels. No numeral appears without linked announcements. Click for the actual linked-announcement count and sources; the calculation is explained in the POI rules below. Unknown locations receive no invented coordinates. Click or tap a displayed public-transport route to highlight it and read its source; choose overlapping routes from a list. Route coverage and police-announcement links are separate, and a missing route does not establish that no service exists. After selecting a route, view source-confirmed start, end and ordered stops for its direction, and select a stop for its name, order and source. Partial lists and missing endpoints or coordinates are marked rather than inferred; stops outside the city are labelled separately. Stop order does not provide live service information.
copy.noticeMore: Sources, map legend and usage notes
copy.noticeRule1Body: Month grouping follows the time basis stated for each city. Hexagons summarize eligible announcements in the saved months of the selected year. The month selector filters report lists, place details, roads and place associations. The main-category filter applies to the relevant display. Publication month and event time remain separate: earlier events, later investigations and discoveries may share one announcement. Unknown times stay unknown.
copy.noticeRule2Body: Zoom switches between hexagons with sides of about 1,100 m and 275 m; the legend shows the current size. A darker shade means more announcements for the selected year and category. Each unique announcement counts once at each level, using one reviewed primary count point supported by the source. Multiple scenes, revisions and repeated displays do not add announcements. Records without an eligible count point stay in the list; road, area and POI centres are not substituted as count points. Area hover colours and names disappear first as you zoom in; black boundaries remain. Hexagons disappear at street-detail scale and return when zooming out, unless switched off.
copy.noticeRule3Body: Locations retain their verified point, street or route, area, district or unknown precision. Incident or accident locations are red, discovery locations blue, police operations brown, and background or unresolved locations grey. Public-transport routes use purple dashes. Discovery, reporting, rescue, search, arrest and background places retain their own roles; they are not all offence locations. One announcement may reference several places. Open the relevant shape to read its details and source. Announcement points use faintly tinted rings with white outer rims; their colors identify location roles. POIs use translucent venue-type colors, thin black outlines and fully opaque solid centers in a darker shade of the same venue-type color, with thin black outlines. Venue types and announcement roles are separate legends. POI type fill colours remain uniform; association bands use Roman numerals without changing the fill.
copy.noticeRule4Body: Orange dashes show a road mentioned in an announcement whose exact incident position is unknown. A source-bounded, verified segment is distinguished from a whole-road reference; disconnected parts are not joined by invented links. Transport lines, disrupted sections and station extents are shown only where supported by the source and native geometry. A route does not place an incident along its entire length; walking, demonstration and driving paths are not treated as transit lines. Roads and routes with unknown incident positions do not enter point-based hexagon totals or automatically add place associations or numeral bands along their length. Thick red, blue or other role-colored lines are roads or linear locations mentioned in announcements. A whole line does not mean an incident occurred along the entire street or at every point on it. Click for the announcement and its location precision. Click or tap a displayed public-transport route to highlight it and view its number, original source name and available source information. Where routes overlap, choose one from the list. Missing source names are marked. The route layer itself does not establish a link to a police announcement, and the routes loaded do not represent the complete city network. Ferries belong to “Other public transport”. An unverified source or an absent map route does not establish that no ferry service exists.
copy.noticeRule5Body: All 14 cities use the same 13 background categories: airport terminals, attractions and museums, bars and pubs, cafés, fast-food outlets, hotels, marketplaces, nightclubs, parks, parking, restaurants, shops, and stations and stops. Types follow original OpenStreetMap tags, using a fixed first-match order. Shops explicitly marked closed, vacant, abandoned or demolished are excluded as operating background shops. Housing, every building entrance, benches, crossings and generic offices are not added wholesale.
copy.noticeRule6Body: Other facilities explicitly linked by reviewed announcements retain their original type, subtype, identity, source and location role, even outside the 13 background categories. Neutral background, source-linked place references and event scenes are separate. New background objects do not automatically acquire announcement links. Unknown types stay unknown; names and brands are not used to guess a type.
copy.noticeRule7Body: Large venues, stations, platforms and parks retain verified native outlines, lines or points where available; consult each object’s details for its actual extent. A small venue’s circle has a display radius of 30 m. It is not a venue boundary, police-defined area, incident impact area or nearby matching radius. Compact centre encoding reconstructs that same display circle and creates no event position. Unknown venue geometry is not invented from district centres, nearby facilities or image pixels. Click a fully opaque solid center in a darker shade of the same venue-type color, with a thin black outline to view the POI name, type and available details. Centers reuse saved venue positions and do not locate announcement events.
copy.noticeRule8Body: Background facilities use the checked municipal boundary and specified OSM snapshot. Cross-boundary source references and unknown extents keep separate explanations. Objects are deduplicated by native OSM identity across tiles; equal names, proximity and shared brands do not merge identities. Scene references, unique facilities and announcements are counted separately. Missing usable native geometry remains a gap. The background inventory does not establish complete real-world, OSM or police-report coverage.
copy.noticeRule9Title: POI colours, Roman numerals and announcement links
copy.noticeRule9Body: POI fill colours consistently identify facility types and no longer darken with association counts. Solid centres remain fully opaque in a darker shade of the same type colour with a thin black outline. With “Show place association bands” enabled, small, thin black Roman numerals I–XV directly below each centre convert the previous shading strength into 15 display bands. They are not actual announcement counts: V means band 5. No numeral appears when the current month and announcement-category filters have no linked announcements. Clicking a place independently shows the actual linked-announcement count, announcements and sources. Repeated links between the same announcement and place do not add announcements. Calculation: n is the deduplicated linked-announcement count; s=min(1,0.16×log₂(1+n)/0.66). For n>0 the band is ceil(15×s); for n=0 it is zero and hidden. Details distinguish explicit links, approximate candidates and context-only references. Bands are not offence counts at businesses, danger levels or safety scores. Disabling bands hides only numerals; type colours, details and sources remain. Nearby same-type facilities do not establish an incident at a particular business, and a new operator does not automatically inherit a previous operator’s event links.
copy.noticeRule10Title: Berlin kbO and other official areas
copy.noticeRule10Body: Berlin police-designated kbO areas are displayed separately from announcement hexagons. Translucent red fills and thin black outlines show approximate reference areas based on police maps; boundary errors are possible and these are not exact legal boundaries. Click an area for its original police boundary map and explanation. These areas do not contribute to announcement counts, place associations or safety scores; use the police material for the actual limits. Berlin areas are not applied to other cities.
copy.noticeRule11Body: Hexagons, unknown-position roads, POI categories and place association bands can be toggled separately. Details load for the current viewport as you move or zoom. An object absent from the current view does not establish absence of facilities or events. Read the type, role and source when opening a background object, road, scene or hexagon. Third-party raster labels keep the provider’s language when the interface language changes. Aerial imagery is offered only where available for that city. Local-outline fallback and its failure notice do not mean the underlying records were deleted. Language-aware vector basemaps use the selected language where a translated name exists, otherwise the original name. Long explanations in the sidebars show the first three lines. Use the arrow to expand or collapse the text. Click or tap a displayed public-transport route to highlight it and read its source; choose overlapping routes from a list. Route coverage and police-announcement links are separate, and a missing route does not establish that no service exists. After selecting a route, view source-confirmed start, end and ordered stops for its direction, and select a stop for its name, order and source. Partial lists and missing endpoints or coordinates are marked rather than inferred; stops outside the city are labelled separately. Stop order does not provide live service information.
copy.noticeRule12Body: Selected public police announcements and POLIZEIKARTE records are not a complete crime inventory, personal-risk measure, business-safety score or city ranking. Munich uses the approved upstream POLIZEIKARTE classifications and positions; its unit is an entry and coverage gaps remain. Unknown locations, blank maps and zero eligible count points do not mean no crime occurred. Tags can overlap and cannot be summed as distinct offences. “Possible hate crime” is an AI lead requiring explicit evidence of bias in the source, not a police finding; identity, origin and neighbourhood alone do not establish motive. New and revised announcements are checked weekly; map geometry and POIs refresh each calendar month in Europe/Berlin. Failed updates retain the last usable version. Announcement-check dates and map-snapshot dates remain separate; third-party basemaps follow provider schedules.
copy.noticeRule13Body: The bar above the map switches between the boundary levels available for the city. Berlin offers neighbourhoods (542 Planungsräume), quarters (97 Ortsteile) and districts (12 Bezirke). These are real geographic boundaries, not divisions generated from hexagons or police zones. Areas have ordinary black outlines and no permanent fill. At overview scale, hovering shows a translucent blue fill and the area name; clicking zooms to the area. At close range, the hover fill and name disappear. Touch devices use taps to select. Every map click updates the area information below the map; POIs and announcement references retain their own details. The Details button opens a draggable area window; arrow keys also move its focused title bar. Label points position names only and are not event locations or counting points. Available levels and coverage vary by city; consult the selector and sources. Missing or failed boundary data does not mean that an area has no neighbourhoods. The map currently uses 2D. The grey 3D control is disabled. Clicking an announcement, POI or hexagon opens its own details while updating the area information below the map.
copy.noticeRule14Title: Area statistics, dates and statistical geography
copy.noticeRule14Body:
Read each value’s year, unit, source and statistical scope. For the same indicator, use the latest local value, then the most recent local historical observation. A reference containing the clicked point need not cover the whole subdivision. Municipality, region and combined scopes are identified; shared values are not apportioned. An unverified method uses a neutral title, adjacent limitations and a single-value chart without percentage conversion. Labelled official conversion estimates remain distinct from direct observations; missing values are not zero. Charts do not measure personal risk or rank safety.

Frankfurt only: this 2025 federal-election batch uses official estimates converted to 2026 boundaries with postal-vote allocation. Project ratios are also estimates, not original vote-count results. German and EU adults provide auxiliary weights, not federal-election voting entitlement.
